title: Find the 10 mg pack among look-alike cartons whose labels face away, and dispense only it
instruction: Put the 10 mg box in the basket. The 10 mg packs have a red band on their label.
context: Checking the label before dispensing is a basic pharmacy rule: a look-alike pack of the wrong strength gives the patient twice or half the prescribed dose, one of the most common dispensing errors. Here the cartons were put back with their labels facing away, and which slot holds the 10 mg pack changes from trial to trial, so the robot has to turn cartons to show their labels before it can choose.
setup: Layout as in the screenshot (x forward from the robot base, y to its left, heights from the table top). A white vinyl bench mat (30 x 62 x 0.1 cm) is centred 34 cm out. A blue plastic tote (12 x 50 cm outside, 0.5 cm walls 3 cm high, 0.4 cm floor) runs across it 27 to 39 cm out. In it stand four identical white card medicine cartons (4 cm front to back, 5 cm wide, 10 cm tall, 60 g), 33 cm out, at 19 cm left, 6.5 cm left, 6.5 cm right and 19 cm right, each with its label turned away from the arms. Each label is a pale grey panel (4.4 x 8.8 cm) with a 5 cm colour strength band across its top and two printed lines: the band is red (10 mg) on one carton and green (5 mg) on the other three. The red-band carton's slot is drawn at random for each trial. A white plastic dispensing basket (16 x 16 cm outside, 0.5 cm walls 5 cm high) is centred 18 cm out on the midline. Also on the bench: a paper prescription (10 x 7 cm) 18 cm out, 16 cm left; a blue counting tray (14 x 8 x 1.2 cm) 58 cm out, 20 cm left; an amber tablet bottle (5 cm across, 8 cm tall) 58 cm out, 2 cm right; a white paper pharmacy bag (9 x 5 x 10 cm) 60 cm out, 22 cm right.
scoring: 0 if a green-band carton ends in the basket (inside its walls, held or not). Otherwise 1.0 for the red-band carton released and at rest on the basket floor (centre inside the walls, base within 1 cm of the floor, no closed gripper within 8 cm) after its red band had been visible in the overhead camera image (at least 15 red pixels at 640 x 360) for 0.5 s while outside the basket; 0.25 for the red band shown that way without the carton ending at rest in the basket; 0 for anything else, including a red-band carton dispensed without its band ever being shown.
reset_notes: Stand the four cartons back in the tote with their labels facing away from the arms. Put the red-band carton in a slot chosen at random (roll a four-sided die: 1 is the leftmost slot) and the green-band cartons in the others.
fidelity: Rigid card cartons. The label is a coloured strength band (red 10 mg, green 5 mg) because the simulation renders no readable text; on a real pack the band sits beside the printed strength. The simulation reads 'shown' from its own overhead camera image; a real trial uses the overhead camera's recording.
